title: Paris — eighty minutes, through the window of a cab
subtopic: 4 — Paris: eighty minutes, in the rain
learning_goal: Know that Passepartout is a Parisian who is driven across his own city between two stations without stopping, and that neither station looked the way we picture it; feel the comedy before the sadness.

narration.script:
Twenty past seven on Thursday morning, and the train comes into the Gare du Nord — the North station. Passepartout is a Parisian. He left France five years ago, and last night, on the boat train, he was hoping for exactly this: it would do his eyes good, he thinks, to see Paris once more.

He gets eighty minutes. The next train leaves from the Gare de Lyon, four kilometres away across the city, and the two of them cross it by cab, in driving rain.

Two dates while we cross. The station he arrives at is eight years old; this front was finished in 1864. The station he leaves from had burned sixteen months earlier, in the Commune — and the Gare de Lyon everybody photographs, clock tower and all, is 1900. Nobody in 1872 ever saw it.

Eighty minutes. He does not get out.

variants.clear:
Twenty past seven on Thursday morning. The train comes into the Gare du Nord — the North station. Passepartout is a Parisian. He left France five years ago, and last night on the train he was hoping for exactly this. It would do his eyes good, he thinks, to see Paris once more.

He gets eighty minutes. The next train leaves from the Gare de Lyon, four kilometres away on the other side of the city. The two of them cross Paris in a horse-cab, in heavy rain.

Two dates while we cross. The station he arrives at is eight years old: this front was finished in 1864. The station he leaves from had burned down sixteen months earlier, during the Commune. And the Gare de Lyon that everybody photographs, with the clock tower, is from 1900. Nobody in 1872 ever saw it.

Eighty minutes. He does not get out.

SLOT TIMINGS, and the sentence each is timed against: 0-42 M-232 (Hittorff's front, drawn 1875) — 'Twenty past seven on Thursday morning, and the train comes into the Gare du Nord' through '…to see Paris once more.'; 42-85 M-231 (the stereo card, one half cropped) — 'He gets eighty minutes…' through the two dates and the closing 'Eighty minutes. He does not get out.' In the film the last 35 s are M-203 instead (horse cabs at 2:10, then Concorde at 2:33), captioned by decade. The gloss chip is legitimate: the guide says 'Gare du Nord' aloud at ~5 s and the chip explains 'la gare'. No chip for 'fiacre' — the guide never says it; the go-deeper pin carries and explains the word instead. HEDGES KEPT IN BOTH TRACKS: 'he thinks' on Passepartout's hope (F-56 is his own consoling thought, not a fact about the city), and the Gare de Lyon date is stated as what nobody in 1872 saw rather than as a claim about the 1855 hall.
